messages:
alex_dev: Karpenter evaluation — should we test migrating our GPU node pools? Looking for quick opinions on provisioners + consolidation behavior.

sam_infra: +1. Worth testing. Karpenter could reduce node-pool sprawl. Main things to validate: GPU AMIs & drivers, driver DaemonSet startup, capacity-type mix (spot vs on-demand), instance family diversity.

chiara_platform: We must be careful about consolidation and drift. cluster-autoscaler has been conservative for our reserved GPU pools; Karpenter's consolidation can reclaim nodes more aggressively which might impact long-running training jobs.

mike_sre: Also remember PDBs and disruption budgets — Karpenter drains respect PDBs but TTL/consolidation thresholds matter. We should configure a safe window to avoid mass evictions during noisy neighbors.

sam_infra: Proposal: spin up a dedicated test cluster in us-west-2 with a single Karpenter provisioner scoped to GPU workloads. Run a canary load that simulates our smallest sustained inference pods (e.g., 200 tokens/sec per pod) and a burst test for scale-up. Track metrics: NodeLaunchTime, PodScheduleLatency, GPU utilization, preemptions.

alex_dev: Agreed. Also need consistent labeling/taints so workloads land on Karpenter-managed nodes. Suggest label `karpenter.sh/capability: gpu` and taint `nvidia.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule`.

sam_infra: Example provisioner we'll start with (very rough): ```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-provisioner
spec:
  requirements:
  - key: karpenter.k8s.aws/capacity-type
    operator: In
    values: [on-demand, spot]
  - key: kubernetes.io/arch
    operator: In
    values: [amd64]
  nodeTemplate:
    labels:
      workload: gpu
    taints:
    - key: nvidia.com/gpu
      value: true
      effect: NoSchedule
  consolidation:
    enabled: true
  limits:
    resources:
      cpu: '2000'
      nvidia.com/gpu: '16'
```
(we'll tune instance selectors after first run)

chiara_platform: Consolidation enabled by default is a red flag for production migration. Recommend: 1) set `ttlSecondsUntilExpired` longer (e.g., 1800s -> 1h), 2) add an annotation opt-out for stateful/long-run GPU jobs, 3) require a canary group before enabling cluster-wide.

mike_sre: From SRE POV instrument these dashboards: NodeLaunchLatency, NodeReadyToSchedTime, PodScheduleWaitTime, PreemptionRate (spot), GPUUtilization per instance. Also run a cost compare: Karpenter packing vs existing nodepools — run A/B for 2 weeks and compare per-token cost and 95/99 latencies.

alex_dev: Ops checklist for the pilot: 1) Bake GPU AMI with packaged drivers + nvidia-device-plugin, 2) Prepare node IAM role for Karpenter, 3) CI job to validate GPU DaemonSet on boot, 4) Ensure spot fallback policy to on-demand, 5) Admission webhook to block oversized unschedulable GPU requests, 6) Add `drift` detection cron to flag instance type mismatches.

sam_infra: I'll create the test cluster and open a PR with the initial provisioner + scripts. Target to spin up next Tue morning and run baseline perf. Will include a `consolidation: disabled` variant first.

chiara_platform: :thumbsup: No objections. Please add me to the PR for consolidation/ttl params.

k8s-bot: deploy-bot: created cluster `karpenter-gpu-test` in us-west-2 (cluster-id: c-kgputest).

alex_dev: Thanks — I'll run the perf harness and post results here. tagging @chiara_platform @mike_sre for metrics review.
